findings.reason: the node would be aimed at the wrong actor, and the only way to make the test read "nothing was stored" is a writer-side refusal the same section forbids, so the section must settle whether the endpoint is a review hold or a writer repair and site the control on the path that actually refuses.
findings.text: the done-when places the refusal at the writer's own entry point ("reads that nothing was stored"), yet the writer's conformance path repairs the departure in place — substituting the canonical equation, the template opening and the locus sentence before persistence — and stores the result, while the refusal §2's prose describes is the documentation review's registry_conformance hold, which runs after the writer has already rewritten and stored the text; a node following this done-when must either rebuild the writer to refuse, which has no home in the plan since line 58 states "no new refusal family is added beside them", or watch the test read a stored, repaired definition and fail.
